newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish SLD-PSL coalition seen after polls - survey.
newsitem.headline: Polish SLD-PSL coalition seen after polls - survey.

text.p: Poland's ruling coalition of ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the Peasant party (PSL) are the most likely parties to form a government following this year's parliamentary polls, a survey showed.
The OBOP state television poll showed on Wednesday that 21 percent of those polled expected the SLD-PSL coalition to remain intact after parliamentary elections, due around September this year.

It showed that 12 percent believed that a coalition between the right-wing Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS), the centrist Union for Freedom (UW) and ultra patriotic Movement for Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) was most likely.
Another 12 percent said a coalition between SLD, UW and the leftist Labour Union (UP) was most probable.
OBOP said that 17 percent wanted a SLD-PSL coalition, while another 17 percent would prefer a AWS-UW-ROP government.
Some 16 percent of the 1,000 adults polled between March 8 and 11 said they most wanted a SLD-UW-UP coalition.
The survey's margin of error is three percent.
